questions.question: When does Easter take place?
questions.explanation: Easter takes place in March or April.
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 4: A modern, thriving society

learning.why_correct_en:
Easter falls in March or April because it is a movable Christian festival. In Western churches, Easter Sunday is the first Sunday after the first full moon following the spring equinox, so its calendar date changes each year.

Common UK customs include Easter Sunday church services, chocolate Easter eggs, Easter Bunny stories and egg hunts. Eggs represent new life and are sometimes linked to the stone at Jesus's tomb. Hot cross buns are traditionally associated with Good Friday; decorated eggs, egg rolling and Easter bonnets also survive in some communities.
learning.why_correct_zh:
正确答案是March or April。Easter是日期会移动的基督教节日；西方教会通常以春分后第一次满月之后的星期日为Easter Sunday，因此每年日期不同。

英国常见习俗包括参加Easter Sunday礼拜、赠送chocolate Easter eggs、讲述Easter Bunny送蛋的故事，以及举行egg hunts。蛋象征new life，也常被联想到耶稣墓门前的石头。Good Friday常吃带十字的hot cross buns；部分地区还保留彩蛋装饰、egg rolling和Easter bonnet等传统。
learning.source_note_zh: 官方教材是答案和考试范围的主要依据；其他权威来源用于补充该主题背景。

questions.question: Where does golf come from?
questions.explanation: The modern game of golf can be traced back to 15th century Scotland.
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 4: A modern, thriving society

learning.why_correct_en:
Modern golf developed in Scotland, but it was not invented by one known person on a single date. It evolved from medieval stick-and-ball games. Players first used streets and churchyards; Scotland's coastal links provided firm, well-drained turf and natural hollows that became hazards, making them ideal places to play a ball through a series of holes.

Scotland's earliest surviving written reference is James II's 1457 ban, issued because golf distracted men from compulsory archery practice. Royal and noble participation later helped move the game onto designated grounds with specialist clubs. The Company of Gentlemen Golfers wrote the earliest surviving 13 rules in Edinburgh in 1744. Early courses had different numbers of holes; the influence of St Andrews and The R&A helped make 18 holes the accepted standard by the late nineteenth century.
learning.why_correct_zh:
正确答案是Scotland。现代golf并非由某个人在某一天突然发明，而是由中世纪苏格兰多种用球杆击球的游戏逐渐发展而来。人们起初曾在街道和教堂墓地击球；苏格兰东海岸称为links的沙质草地排水良好，天然凹地又能形成障碍，因此很适合把球从起点连续打进一系列洞中。

1457年，James II下令禁玩golf，担心它妨碍国民练习国防所需的射箭；这是苏格兰现存最早的高尔夫文字记录。后来王室和贵族参与，使游戏转移到专门场地并使用特制球杆。1744年，Edinburgh的Company of Gentlemen Golfers写下现存最早的13条规则。早期球场洞数不一，随着St Andrews和The R&A影响扩大，18洞到19世纪后期逐渐成为标准。
learning.source_note_zh: 官方教材是答案和考试范围的主要依据；其他权威来源用于补充该主题背景。

questions.question: Complaints against the police can ONLY be made by writing to the Police Complaints Commissioner.
questions.explanation: False. Anyone can make a complaint about the police by going to a police station and writing to the Chief Constable of the police force involved. Complaints can also be made to an independent body: the Independent Police Complaints Commission in England and Wales, the Police Complaints Commissioner for Scotland or the Police Ombudsman for Northern Ireland.
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 5: The UK government, the law and your role

learning.why_correct_en: False. A police complaint is not limited to a written letter to one commissioner. It may be made directly to the police force or through the independent oversight body for the relevant UK nation; the bodies and procedures differ across England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
learning.why_correct_zh: 本题答案是False。投诉警察并非只能写信给一位Police Complaints Commissioner；可直接向有关police force提出，也可通过所在UK地区的独立监督机构办理。England和Wales、Scotland及Northern Ireland的机构与程序不同。

questions.question: Who is the patron Saint of Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: The patron Saint of Northern Ireland is St Patrick.
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 4: A modern, thriving society

learning.why_correct_en:
St Patrick is the patron saint associated with Northern Ireland and Ireland. St Patrick's Day is 17 March, traditionally his death date.

A shamrock is a small clover-like plant with three leaflets at the end of one stalk. The Christian Trinity means that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three distinct persons but one God. A later tradition says that St Patrick held up a shamrock and used its three leaflets on one plant as a simple comparison. This is why the shamrock became closely associated with St Patrick's Day and Ireland, although there is no direct record of the story from Patrick's lifetime.
learning.why_correct_zh:
正确答案是St Patrick。St Patrick’s Day在3月17日举行，传统认为是他的逝世纪念日。

shamrock指常见的三叶草：同一根叶柄顶端分出三片小叶。Christian Trinity（三位一体）指Father（圣父）、Son（圣子）和Holy Spirit（圣灵）是三个不同位格，但同属一位上帝。后世传说称，St Patrick拿着一株shamrock，以“一株植物有三片小叶”作比喻来解释这个概念。因此shamrock后来成为St Patrick’s Day和爱尔兰的重要象征；不过这是流传已久的传统故事，并没有St Patrick本人时代的直接记录。
learning.source_note_zh: 官方教材是答案和考试范围的主要依据；其他权威来源用于补充该主题背景。

options.text: Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Protestant
Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Catholic

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE:
questions.explanation: Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Catholic.
correct_answers: Mary Stuart (‘Mary, Queen of Scots’) was a Catholic
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 3: A long and illustrious history

learning.why_correct_en:
Mary, Queen of Scots was Catholic, while her cousin Elizabeth I was Protestant. Mary's religion and claim to the English throne made her a focus for Catholic plots; after years in English custody, she was executed in 1587.

Catholics and Protestants are both Christians who affirm Jesus Christ, the Bible and the Trinity. The Catholic Church is a worldwide communion led by the Pope and bishops; it receives doctrine through Scripture and Apostolic Tradition, interpreted by the Church's teaching authority, and recognises seven sacraments. Protestant is an umbrella term for many traditions that emerged from the sixteenth-century Reformation. They reject the Pope's universal jurisdiction, place greater emphasis on Scripture as the highest norm and on salvation by God's grace through faith. Many recognise Baptism and Holy Communion as the two principal Gospel sacraments, but Anglican, Presbyterian and other Protestant churches differ considerably in worship and government.
learning.why_correct_zh:
正确说法是Mary, Queen of Scots was a Catholic；她的表亲Elizabeth I是Protestant。Mary的宗教身份和英格兰王位继承主张使她成为Catholic plots的焦点，长期被囚后于1587年处决。

两者都属于Christianity，都相信Jesus Christ、Bible和Trinity。Catholic Church是由Pope与各地主教领导的全球教会；其教义依据Bible和Apostolic Tradition，由教会训导权解释，并承认七件Sacraments。

Protestant是16世纪Reformation后多个教派的总称，并非单一教会；它们不承认Pope对所有基督徒的最高管辖权，更强调Bible是信仰的最高准则，以及人靠上帝的grace、通过faith得救。许多Protestant教会主要承认Baptism和Holy Communion两件圣礼，但Anglican、Presbyterian等教派的组织和礼仪仍有明显差异。

questions.question: William of Orange was asked by Protestants to invade England and proclaim himself king. But, when William reached England, there was no resistance and he took over the throne. This event was later known as:
questions.explanation: William of Orange was asked by Protestants to invade England and proclaim himself king. When William reached England, there was no resistance and he took over the throne. This event was later called the ‘Glorious Revolution’.
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 3: A long and illustrious history

learning.why_correct_en: The event is called the Glorious Revolution of 1688. William of Orange landed with an army, James II lost political and military support and fled, and William III and Mary II accepted the crown subject to the 1689 Bill of Rights, strengthening Parliament's constitutional position.
learning.why_correct_zh: 正确答案是Glorious Revolution。1688年William of Orange率军登陆，James II失去政治与军事支持后逃亡；William III与Mary II随后接受王位及1689年Bill of Rights，使Parliament的宪制地位进一步增强。
learning.source_note_zh: 官方教材是答案和考试范围的主要依据；其他权威来源用于补充该主题背景。

questions.question: If a husband forces his wife to have sex he can be charged with rape.
questions.explanation: This statement is true.
questions.handbook_locator: Chapter 5: The UK government, the law and your role

learning.why_correct_en: True. Marriage does not create permanent consent to sex. A husband who intentionally penetrates his wife without her consent, and without reasonably believing that she consents, can be prosecuted for rape; English law definitively rejected the old marital-rape exemption in 1991.
learning.why_correct_zh: 本题答案是True。婚姻不等于永久同意性行为；丈夫若在妻子未同意且自己并无合理理由相信对方同意时强行发生性行为，可以被控rape。英国法律于1991年明确否定旧有的marital rape exemption。
learning.source_note_zh: 官方教材是答案和考试范围的主要依据；其他权威来源用于补充该主题背景。
